questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a combination reaction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CaO + H2O → Ca(OH)2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Combination Reaction** is a type of chemical reaction where **two or more reactants** (elements or compounds) combine to form a **single product**. The general representation is **A + B → AB**.
 
• **CaO + H2O → Ca(OH)2**: In this reaction, **Calcium Oxide** (also known as **Quick Lime**) reacts vigorously with **Water** to produce **Calcium Hydroxide** (known as **Slaked Lime**). Since two reactants combine to form one single product, it is a classic example of a **Combination Reaction**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Zn + H2SO4 → ZnSO4 + H2**: This reaction involves **Zinc** displacing **Hydrogen** from **Sulphuric Acid**. This is an example of a **Single Displacement Reaction**, not a combination reaction. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **2KClO3 → 2KCl + 3O2**: In this case, a single reactant, **Potassium Chlorate**, breaks down into two simpler products, **Potassium Chloride** and **Oxygen**, usually upon heating. This is a **Decomposition Reaction**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **CuSO4 + BaCl2 → BaSO4 + CuCl2**: This reaction involves the exchange of ions between **Copper(II) Sulphate** and **Barium Chloride** to form **Barium Sulphate** and **Copper(II) Chloride**. It is categorized as a **Double Displacement Reaction** or a **Precipitation Reaction**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is CaO + H2O → Ca(OH)2.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Exothermic Nature of Combination Reactions:** Many combination reactions, such as the reaction of **Quick Lime** with **Water**, release a significant amount of heat. Such reactions are called **Exothermic Reactions**. This specific reaction is used in **whitewashing** walls, where the **Slaked Lime** reacts slowly with **Carbon Dioxide** in the air to form a thin layer of **Calcium Carbonate**.
 
• **Decomposition Reactions:** These are the opposite of combination reactions. A single substance splits into two or more substances. This process usually requires energy in the form of **heat** (Thermal Decomposition), **light** (Photolysis), or **electricity** (Electrolysis). For example, the electrolysis of **Water (H2O)** yields **Hydrogen** and **Oxygen** gases.
 
• **Displacement Reactions:** A more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound. The **Reactivity Series** is used to determine which metal can displace another. For instance, **Iron (Fe)** can displace **Copper (Cu)** from a **Copper Sulphate (CuSO4)** solution because Iron is more reactive.
 
• **Double Displacement Reactions:** These occur when two ionic compounds in solution react by exchanging their **cations** and **anions**. Often, one of the products formed is an **insoluble solid** called a **precipitate**, as seen with **Barium Sulphate (BaSO4)** in the reaction between Barium Chloride and sodium sulphate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chemical Equations:** A chemical equation must always be **balanced** to satisfy the **Law of Conservation of Mass**, which states that mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.
 
• **Oxidation and Reduction (Redox):** Most chemical reactions also involve the transfer of electrons. **Oxidation** is the gain of **Oxygen** or loss of **Hydrogen/Electrons**, while **Reduction** is the loss of **Oxygen** or gain of **Hydrogen/Electrons**.
 
• **Physical States:** In chemical equations, symbols like **(s)** for solid, **(l)** for liquid, **(g)** for gas, and **(aq)** for aqueous (dissolved in water) are used to provide more information about the reaction conditions.

questions.question: The potential energy acquired by a balloon when we press it (changing its shape), or by a spring inside a toy car when wound, is possessed by virtue of the object's ____________.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Potential Energy** is defined as the energy possessed by an object by virtue of its **position** relative to others, **stresses** within itself, its **electric charge**, or its **configuration**.
 
• When we press a **balloon**, we apply an **external force** that changes its **shape**. This change in **physical arrangement** or **configuration** stores energy within the balloon's material. ***Hence, the mention of changing shape relates directly to configuration.***
 
• A **spring** inside a **toy car**, when **wound**, undergoes a change in its **coiling structure**. The work done in winding the spring is stored as **Elastic Potential Energy** due to the altered **configuration** of the metal coils.
 
• The term **configuration** in physics refers to the **relative positions** of the constituent particles of a system or the **geometrical shape** of an object.
 
• This energy remains **stored** as long as the object is held in that specific state and is **released** when the object is allowed to return to its original form, often converting into **Kinetic Energy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Potential Energy:**
 
 
• **Gravitational Potential Energy**: This is energy stored in an object due to its **vertical position** or **height**. The **numerical value** is calculated using the formula **P.E. = mgh**, where **m** is **mass**, **g** is **acceleration due to gravity** (approx **9.8 m/s²**), and **h** is **height**.
 
• **Elastic Potential Energy**: Stored in materials that can be **stretched** or **compressed**, such as **rubber bands**, **trampolines**, or **springs**.
 
• **Chemical Potential Energy**: Stored in the **chemical bonds** of substances, like in **batteries**, **food**, or **fuel**.
 
 
 
• **Kinetic Energy:**
 
 
• This is the energy of **motion**. An object moving at a **constant speed** possesses kinetic energy defined by the **mass** and the **square of its velocity** (**K.E. = 1/2 mv²**).
 
• Unlike potential energy, kinetic energy cannot be stored; it is **actively used** during motion.
 
 
 
• **Mechanical Energy:**
 
 
• The **sum** of potential and kinetic energy in a system is called **Mechanical Energy**. According to the **Law of Conservation of Energy**, the total mechanical energy in an **isolated system** remains **constant**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Configuration vs. Position:** While **position** usually refers to the **location** of an object in a **gravitational field**, **configuration** refers to the **internal arrangement** or **deformation** of the object itself.
 
• **Unit of Energy:** The **S.I. unit** of energy is the **Joule (J)**, named after the English physicist **James Prescott Joule**. One Joule is equal to the **work done** by a **force** of **one Newton** acting through a **distance** of **one meter**.
 
• **Factors affecting Elastic Potential Energy:** It depends on the **spring constant (k)**, which represents the **stiffness** of the material, and the **displacement (x)** or the amount of **deformation** applied.
 
• **Historical Context:** The concept of **Potential Energy** was formally introduced in the **19th century** by the Scottish engineer and physicist **William Rankine**.

questions.question: What is the primary reason ores are enriched prior to the extraction of metals?

options.text: To alter the internal crystal structure of the ore for conversion
To improve the final metal's resistance to corrosion and rust
To enhance the melting point of the mineral content for refining
To eliminate earthy impurities such as sand and unwanted rock

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To eliminate earthy impurities such as sand and unwanted rock**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Ores mined from the earth are seldom pure; they are usually contaminated with large amounts of unwanted materials such as **soil**, **sand**, **clay**, and **stony matter**. These impurities are collectively referred to as **gangue**.
 
• The process used to remove these impurities from the ore before the metal is extracted is known as **enrichment of ore** or **concentration of ore**. ***Hence, the primary reason for enrichment is to eliminate earthy impurities like sand and rock, making option 4 correct.***
 
• The extraction of metal from a concentrated ore is chemically and economically more feasible than extracting it directly from the raw mined ore.
 
• Various techniques for **enrichment** are selected based on the differences between the **physical** or **chemical properties** of the ore and the **gangue**.
 
• Common physical methods of enrichment include **hydraulic washing** (based on gravity), **magnetic separation** (based on magnetic properties), and **froth flotation** (specifically for sulfide ores).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hydraulic Washing:** This is a type of **gravity separation**. It is based on the difference in the specific gravities of the **ore** and the **gangue** particles. It is frequently used for **heavy oxide ores** like **hematite** (iron ore) and **tin stone**.
 
• **Froth Flotation Process:** This method is predominantly used for the enrichment of **sulfide ores** (e.g., **Copper pyrites**, **Galena**). It relies on the principle that ore particles are wetted by **oils** (like pine oil) while gangue particles are wetted by **water**.
 
• **Magnetic Separation:** This method is applied when either the **ore** or the **impurities** possess **magnetic properties**. For example, **Magnetite** (an iron ore) can be separated from non-magnetic gangue using a magnetic roller.
 
• **Leaching:** This is a **chemical method** of enrichment. The ore is treated with a suitable **reagent** (like **Sodium Hydroxide** for **Bauxite**) that dissolves the ore but leaves the impurities insoluble.
 
• **Analysis of Other Options:**
 
 
• **Option 1:** Altering internal crystal structure occurs during processes like **calcination** or **roasting** (thermal treatment), not enrichment. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Option 2:** Improving resistance to **corrosion** and **rust** is achieved after extraction through **alloying**, **galvanizing**, or **painting**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Option 3:** In metallurgy, **fluxes** are often added to **lower** the melting point of impurities, not to enhance the melting point of the mineral content. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The entire scientific and technological process used for the isolation of the metal from its ores is known as **metallurgy**.
 
• **Roasting:** This is the process of heating **sulfide ores** strongly in the presence of **excess air** to convert them into **oxides**.
 
• **Calcination:** This involves heating **carbonate ores** or hydrated oxides in the **absence** or limited supply of air to remove moisture and volatile impurities, converting them into oxides.
 
• **Reduction:** Once the ore is enriched and converted to an oxide, it is reduced to the **metallic state** using reducing agents like **carbon (coke)**, **carbon monoxide**, or through **electrolysis** for highly reactive metals like **Aluminum** and **Sodium**.
</ul

questions.question: What makes cartilage more flexible than bone in the human body?

options.text: It contains a solid, protein-rich matrix.
It contains a matrix filled with fat.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It contains a fluid-like matrix.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cartilage** is a specialized type of **connective tissue** that provides structural support while remaining significantly more flexible than bone.
 
• Unlike the hard and rigid matrix of bones, the matrix of cartilage is composed of proteins and sugars which, in certain physiological contexts, is described as **fluid-like** or semi-solid, allowing it to be compressed and bent without breaking. ***Hence, the correct answer is option 2.***
 
• It consists of widely spaced cells called **chondrocytes**, which are embedded in the extensive extracellular matrix.
 
• Cartilage is found in various parts of the human body, including the **joints** between bones, the **rib cage**, the **ear**, the **nose**, the **bronchial tubes**, and the **intervertebral discs**.
 
• Its primary function is to smoothen bone surfaces at **joints** and provide a flexible framework for structures like the **trachea** and **larynx**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• Bones have a hard, non-flexible matrix rich in **calcium** and **phosphorus** compounds.
 
• The cells of the bone, called **osteocytes**, are embedded in this hard matrix, providing the body with its primary structural framework.
 
 
 
• **Tendons and Ligaments**:
 
 
• **Tendons** are fibrous connective tissues that **join muscles to bones**. They have great strength but limited flexibility. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect as it describes tendons.***
 
• **Ligaments** connect **bone to bone** and are very elastic with considerable strength.
 
 
 
• **Adipose Tissue**:
 
 
• This tissue is specialized for **fat storage** and is found below the skin and between internal organs.
 
• It acts as an **insulator** and a protective cushion for the body. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect as it describes adipose tissue.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Avascular Nature**: One of the most important features of cartilage is that it is **avascular**, meaning it does not contain **blood vessels**. Nutrients must diffuse through the matrix to reach the cells, which is why cartilage heals more slowly than bone.
 
• **Types of Cartilage**:
 
 
• **Hyaline Cartilage**: The most common type, found on the ends of long bones at **joints**.
 
• **Elastic Cartilage**: Contains more elastic fibers, providing great flexibility to the **external ear (pinna)**.
 
• **Fibrocartilage**: The strongest type, found in the **intervertebral discs** to act as a shock absorber.
 
 
 
• **Ossification**: During the developmental stage of a human **embryo**, much of the skeleton is made of cartilage, which is later replaced by bone through the process of **ossification** as the individual grows.

questions.question: Which of the following rules can be used to determine the direction of magnetic field due to a current carrying circular loop?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right Hand Thumb Rule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Right Hand Thumb Rule**, also known as **Maxwell’s Corkscrew Rule**, is a fundamental principle used to determine the direction of the **magnetic field** associated with a **current-carrying conductor**, including a **circular loop**.
 
• According to this rule, if you imagine holding the current-carrying wire in your **right hand** such that your **thumb** points in the direction of the **electric current**, then your **curled fingers** will point in the direction of the **magnetic field lines**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• In the case of a **circular loop**, the magnetic field lines near the wire are in the form of **concentric circles**. As we move towards the **center of the loop**, the arcs of these big circles appear as **straight lines**.
 
• Every section of the wire contributes to the magnetic field lines in the same direction within the loop. At the **center of the circular loop**, the magnetic field is **perpendicular** to the plane of the loop.
 
• The strength of the magnetic field produced by a current-carrying wire at a given point depends directly on the **magnitude of the current (I)** passing through it and inversely on the **distance (r)** from the wire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fleming’s Left Hand Rule:**
 
 
• This rule is primarily used to find the direction of the **magnetic force** acting on a moving **charge** or a **current-carrying conductor** placed in an external **magnetic field**.
 
• It is commonly applied in the working of an **electric motor**.
 
• The **forefinger** represents the **field**, the **middle finger** represents the **current**, and the **thumb** represents the **motion or force**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Fleming’s Right Hand Rule:**
 
 
• This rule is used to determine the direction of the **induced current** when a conductor moves inside a **magnetic field**.
 
• It is the basis for the operation of an **electric generator**.
 
• The **thumb** shows the **direction of motion**, the **forefinger** shows the **field**, and the **middle finger** shows the direction of the **induced current**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Maxwell’s Left Hand Rule:**
 
 
• There is no widely recognized "Maxwell's Left Hand Rule" in standard electromagnetism for determining field directions. James Clerk Maxwell is specifically associated with the **Right-Hand Corkscrew Rule**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Clock-Face Rule:** A simple method to find the **polarity** of a **circular loop**. If the current flows in an **anti-clockwise** direction, the face of the loop behaves like a **North Pole**. If the current flows in a **clockwise** direction, the face behaves like a **South Pole**.
 
• **Number of Turns:** If there is a circular coil having **n turns**, the field produced is **n times** as large as that produced by a single turn. This is because the current in each circular turn has the same direction, and the field due to each turn then just adds up.
 
• **Magnetic Field Formula:** For a circular loop of **radius R** carrying **current I**, the magnetic field **(B)** at the center is given by **B = (μ₀I) / (2R)**, where **μ₀** is the **permeability of free space**.

• In some species, the **thalamus** undergoes significant development post-fertilization to become a fleshy, edible part of the **fruit**, such as in **Apples** and **Pears**.
 
• **Ovules** are the structures that develop into seeds; they are formed and housed within the **ovary** of the **carpel**, not the thalamus. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Nectar** is a sugar-rich liquid produced by specialized glands called **nectaries**. While nectaries are often located on the **thalamus**, the thalamus itself is not the producing tissue. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Pollen grains** are the male microgametophytes of seed plants, which are produced within the **pollen sacs** of the **anther**, a component of the **stamen**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

• **Classification based on Thalamus Position:**
 
 
• **Hypogynous Flowers:** The **thalamus** is convex or conical. The **ovary** occupies the highest position while other parts are situated below it. Examples include **Mustard**, **Brinjal**, and **China Rose**.
 
• **Perigynous Flowers:** The **thalamus** forms a rim or cup-like structure around the **ovary**. The ovary is said to be **half-inferior**. Examples include **Rose**, **Peach**, and **Plum**.

• In **Angiosperms**, the successful attachment of the **gynoecium** to the **thalamus** is critical for nutrient transfer from the vegetative plant body to the developing **embryo**.

</ul

questions.question: What is the primary function of the dendrites in a neuron?

options.text: To transmit signals from the axon to the cell body

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To transmit signals from the axon to the cell body**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dendrites** are the specialized, branch-like protoplasmic extensions of a **nerve cell** (neuron) that function as the primary **receptive units** of the cell.
 
• The primary role of **dendrites** is to receive **electrochemical signals** (neurotransmitters) from the **axons** of neighboring neurons and conduct them toward the **cell body**, also known as the **soma**. ***Hence, the statement in option 2 is correct.***
 
• Structure-wise, **dendrites** are highly branched, forming what is known as a **dendritic tree**. This extensive branching increases the **surface area** available for **synaptic connections**, allowing a single neuron to process information from thousands of other cells.
 
• While **dendrites** receive signals, they do not typically generate the main **action potential**; instead, they carry **graded potentials**. These are small electrical changes that accumulate at the **axon hillock** to determine if an impulse will be fired. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect as the axon hillock, not the dendrite, creates the main impulse.***
 
• **Dendrites** do not serve a primary protective role; protection and metabolic support are provided by **glial cells** (such as **astrocytes** and **oligodendrocytes**) and the **myelin sheath**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• The **synapse** is the junction between the **axon terminal** of one neuron and the **dendrite** of another. While dendrites are part of this structure, their "function" is the transmission of the signal rather than the mere formation of the gap itself. ***Hence, statement 1 is less accurate than statement 2.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of a Neuron:**
 
 
• **Soma (Cell Body):** Contains the **nucleus** and **organelles**. it integrates incoming signals from the **dendrites** to "decide" whether to pass the signal along.
 
• **Axon:** A long, cable-like projection that carries **nerve impulses** (action potentials) **away** from the cell body toward other neurons, muscles, or glands.
 
• **Axon Terminals:** Located at the end of the axon, these release **neurotransmitters** into the **synaptic cleft** to communicate with the next **dendrite**.
 
 
 
• **Signal Transmission Process:**
 
 
• The flow of information in a **neuron** is strictly **unidirectional**: it enters through the **dendrites**, passes through the **soma**, travels down the **axon**, and exits via the **axon terminals**.
 
• In the **Central Nervous System (CNS)**, this communication allows for complex functions such as **reflexes**, **memory**, and **motor control**.
 
 
 
• **Myelin Sheath:**
 
 
• This is a fatty insulating layer formed by **Schwann cells** in the **Peripheral Nervous System**. It speeds up **signal conduction** through a process called **saltatory conduction**, where the impulse "jumps" between **Nodes of Ranvier**.
 
 
 
• **Classification of Neurons:**
 
 
• **Sensory Neurons:** Carry information from **sensory receptors** (like skin or eyes) toward the **brain**.
 
• **Motor Neurons:** Transmit commands from the **brain** or **spinal cord** to **muscles** and **glands**.
 
• **Interneurons:** Found within the **brain** and **spinal cord**, they connect sensory and motor neurons and handle complex **information processing**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Neuroplasticity:** The **dendritic spines** (small protrusions on dendrites) can change in shape, size, and number in response to **learning** and **experience**, a phenomenon known as **synaptic plasticity**.
 
• **Neurotransmitters:** Common chemicals involved in **dendritic reception** include **Glutamate** (excitatory), **GABA** (inhibitory), **Acetylcholine**, and **Dopamine**.
 
• **Diseases:** Damage to **dendrites** or their **synapses** is a hallmark of several **neurodegenerative diseases**, such as **Alzheimer’s disease** and **Parkinson’s disease**, which disrupt the efficient **transmission of signals** in the **human brain**.

questions.question: Which of the following is a converging lens?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Convex lens**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **convex lens** is also known as a **converging lens** because it causes parallel rays of light passing through it to **refract** inward and meet (converge) at a single point known as the **principal focus**.
 
• Structurally, a **convex lens** is **thicker at the center** and **thinner at the edges**. This specific shape allows the lens to bend light rays toward the **optical axis**.
 
• The distance from the **optical center** of the lens to the **principal focus** is defined as the **focal length**. For a converging lens, the **focal length** is always considered **positive** in sign conventions.
 
• These lenses have the unique ability to form both **real** and **virtual** images. When an object is placed beyond the **focus**, the image produced is **real and inverted**. However, if the object is placed between the **focus** and the **optical center**, the image is **virtual, erect, and magnified**.
 
• The **power of a lens** is the reciprocal of its **focal length** in meters. Since a **convex lens** has a positive focal length, its **optical power** is also **positive**, measured in **Dioptres (D)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Concave Lens**:
 
 
• Commonly referred to as a **diverging lens**, it is thinner at the center than at the edges.
 
• It causes parallel light rays to spread out or **diverge**. The rays appear to originate from a **virtual focus** located in front of the lens.
 
• It always produces a **virtual, erect, and diminished** image regardless of the object's position. It is used to correct **Myopia** (short-sightedness).
 
 
 
• **Cylindrical Lens**:
 
 
• A **cylindrical lens** focuses light into a **line** rather than a point, as it has different radii of curvature in the horizontal and vertical planes.
 
• It is primarily used in **optometry** to correct **astigmatism**, a condition where the **cornea** or lens of the eye has an irregular curvature.
 
 
 
• **Planoconcave Lens**:
 
 
• This lens features one **flat (plano)** surface and one **inwardly curved (concave)** surface.
 
• It is a type of **diverging lens** with a **negative focal length**. It is frequently used in **optical systems** to expand light beams or to increase the focal length of other lens groups.
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications**:
 
 
• **Convex lenses** are utilized in **magnifying glasses**, **microscopes**, **telescopes**, and **camera lenses**.
 
• In the **human eye**, the **crystalline lens** is a natural **convex lens** that focuses light onto the **retina**.
 
• They are also used in **spectacles** to treat **Hypermetropia** (long-sightedness), helping the eye focus images correctly on the **retina** instead of behind it.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Lens Formula** is expressed as **1/f = 1/v - 1/u**, where **f** is the **focal length**, **v** is the **image distance**, and **u** is the **object distance**.
 
• **Magnification (m)** for a lens is the ratio of **image height** to **object height**, also given by **v/u**. For a **convex lens**, the magnification can be **greater than, equal to, or less than 1**.
 
• The **Lens Maker's Formula** relates the **focal length** to the **refractive index** of the material and the **radii of curvature** of the two surfaces, which is essential for manufacturing **corrective eyewear** and **optical instruments**.
</ul

questions.question: When an acid reacts with a base, which of the following is/are always formed, regardless of the specific acid or base used?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Salt and water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The reaction between an **acid** and a **base** is fundamentally known as a **neutralization reaction**.
 
• During this process, the **hydrogen ions (H+)** from the acid react with the **hydroxide ions (OH-)** from the base to produce **water (H2O)**.
 
• The **cation** from the base and the **anion** from the acid combine to form an ionic compound called a **salt**.
 
• This outcome is universal for all acid-base reactions; whether the reactants are **strong** or **weak**, the formation of **salt and water** is the characteristic result.
 
• Neutralization reactions are typically **exothermic** in nature, meaning they release **heat energy** to the surroundings during the chemical change.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Common Examples**:
 
 
• A classic example is the reaction between **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)** and **Sodium hydroxide (NaOH)**, which produces **Sodium chloride (NaCl)**, commonly known as table salt, and **water**.
 
• Another example is the reaction between **Sulfuric acid (H2SO4)** and **Potassium hydroxide (KOH)** to form **Potassium sulfate (K2SO4)** and water.
 
 
 
• **pH Levels**:
 
 
• If a **strong acid** reacts with a **strong base**, the resulting salt solution is **neutral**, having a **pH of 7**.
 
• If a **strong acid** reacts with a **weak base**, the resulting salt will be **acidic** (pH less than 7).
 
• Conversely, a **weak acid** reacting with a **strong base** will produce a **basic salt** (pH greater than 7).
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications**:
 
 
• In **medicine**, individuals suffering from acidity take **antacids**, which are mild bases like **Magnesium hydroxide [Mg(OH)2]**, to neutralize excess **Hydrochloric acid** in the stomach.
 
• In **agriculture**, if the soil is too acidic, farmers treat it with **Quick lime (Calcium oxide)** or **Slaked lime (Calcium hydroxide)** to neutralize the acidity and improve **crop yield**.
 
• In **industry**, factory wastes which are often acidic are neutralized with basic substances before being discharged into **water bodies** to protect **aquatic life**.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Equation**: The general word equation for this process is represented as: **Acid + Base → Salt + Water**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes image formation by a convex mirror?

options.text: When the object is at infinity, the image is formed at the focus, real and inverted.
When the object is at infinity, the image is formed at the pole and is real and inverted.
When the object is at a finite distance, the image is formed between the pole and focus, virtual and diminished.
When the object is at a finite distance, the image is formed beyond the centre of curvature, real and enlarged.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**When the object is at a finite distance, the image is formed between the pole and focus, virtual and diminished.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **convex mirror**, also known as a **diverging mirror**, has a reflecting surface that bulges outward toward the light source. It always forms a **virtual, erect, and diminished** image of a real object, regardless of the object's position.
 
• **Statement 1**: When the object is at **infinity**, the incident rays are parallel to the principal axis. After reflection, they appear to diverge from the **principal focus (F)** located **behind the mirror**. The image formed is **virtual, erect, and highly diminished** (point-sized). *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect because it mentions the image is real and inverted.*
 
• **Statement 2**: For an object at **infinity**, the image is always formed at the **focus (F)**, not the **pole (P)**. Furthermore, a convex mirror cannot produce a **real and inverted** image for a real object. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• **Statement 3**: When the object is placed at a **finite distance** (anywhere between the pole and infinity), the reflected rays diverge, and their backward extensions intersect between the **Pole (P)** and the **Focus (F)** behind the mirror. The resulting image is **virtual**, **erect**, and **diminished** in size. *Hence, statement 3 is correct.*
 
• **Statement 4**: In a convex mirror, the image is always formed **behind the mirror** within the focal length. It is never formed **beyond the centre of curvature (C)**, nor can it be **real and enlarged** for a real object. *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mirror Formula**: The mathematical relationship between the object distance (**u**), image distance (**v**), and the focal length (**f**) is expressed as **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**. For a convex mirror, the **focal length (f)** is always **positive**.
 
• **Linear Magnification (m)**: This is defined as the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object (**h'/h**), which also equals **-v/u**. For convex mirrors, the value of **m** is always **positive** (indicating an erect image) and **less than 1** (indicating a diminished image).
 
• **Applications**: Due to their ability to produce an **erect image** and provide a **wider field of view**, convex mirrors are primarily used as **rear-view mirrors** in **vehicles** such as cars, trucks, and motorcycles. They are also used as **security mirrors** in shops and **blind-spot mirrors** on sharp road curves.
 
• **Sign Convention**: According to the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**, distances measured in the direction of incident light are **positive**. Since the **Focus** and **Centre of Curvature** of a convex mirror lie behind the reflecting surface, their distances from the **Pole** are taken as **positive** values.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Diverging Nature**: A convex mirror is called a **diverging mirror** because it spreads out parallel light rays that strike its surface. This is why the **focus** is **virtual**, as rays only "appear" to meet there when traced backward.
 
• **Image Characteristics**: Unlike a **concave mirror**, which can form real, virtual, enlarged, or diminished images depending on the **object position**, a **convex mirror** is restricted to forming only **virtual, erect, and diminished** images of real objects.
 
• **Range of Image**: The image in a convex mirror always moves from the **Focus (F)** toward the **Pole (P)** as the object is brought closer to the mirror from **infinity**, but it never crosses the pole to the front of the mirror.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following activities best demonstrates that there is a force of attraction between particles of matter?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Breaking a chalk stick**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Particles of matter have **force of attraction** acting between them. This force keeps the particles together. The strength of this force of attraction varies from one kind of matter to another.
 
• **Compressing a sponge**: When we compress a sponge, we are actually pushing out the **air** trapped in the **minute holes** (pores) of the sponge. This activity primarily demonstrates that matter (like solids) can have **spaces** between particles or trapped air, rather than the force of attraction between the particles of the sponge material itself. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Dissolving sugar in water**: This activity demonstrates that there are **enough spaces** between the particles of matter. When sugar dissolves in water, the **sugar particles** get into the spaces between the **water particles**. This is an example of **diffusion** and the presence of intermolecular spaces. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Breaking a chalk stick**: When we try to break a chalk stick, we need to apply **external force** to overcome the **internal force of attraction** that holds the particles together. The fact that it requires effort to separate the particles into smaller pieces directly proves that there is a force holding them in a **fixed structure**. Different substances like **iron nails**, **rubber bands**, and **chalk** require different amounts of force to break, indicating different strengths of attraction. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• **Heating ice to form water**: This activity demonstrates the **effect of temperature** on the **physical state** of matter. Heating provides **kinetic energy** to the particles, allowing them to overcome the forces of attraction, but the act of "breaking" a solid is a more direct mechanical demonstration of the existing force. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nature of Particles**: Matter is made up of very **small particles** (atoms or molecules). These particles are so small that they cannot be seen with the naked eye. This was famously demonstrated by the **dilution of potassium permanganate** in water.
 
• **Characteristics of Particles**:
 
 
• Particles of matter have **space** between them (Intermolecular space).
 
• Particles of matter are **continuously moving** (Kinetic energy).
 
• Particles of matter **attract** each other (Intermolecular force).
 
 
 
• **Intermolecular Force of Attraction**:
 
 
• In **Solids**, the force of attraction is **maximum**, which is why they have a **definite shape** and **volume**.
 
• In **Liquids**, the force of attraction is **intermediate**, allowing particles to slide over each other.
 
• In **Gases**, the force of attraction is **minimum** (negligible), allowing particles to move freely in any direction.
 
 
 
• **Diffusion**: The **intermixing of particles** of two different types of matter on their own is called diffusion. The rate of diffusion increases with an **increase in temperature** because particles gain more **kinetic energy** and move faster.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Cohesive Forces**: The force of attraction between particles of the **same substance** is known as **cohesion**. This is what keeps a **water drop** spherical or a **chalk stick** intact.
 
• **Adhesive Forces**: The force of attraction between particles of **different substances** is called **adhesion**. This allows **ink** to stick to paper or **water** to wet a glass surface.
 
• **Physical State Change**: When we heat a solid, the **vibrations** of the particles increase. At the **melting point**, the heat energy overcomes the **forces of attraction** between the particles, and the solid converts into a liquid. This temperature remains constant during the change of state due to **Latent Heat of Fusion**.
 
• **Compressibility**: This is the property of being reduced in volume by **pressure**. **Gases** are highly compressible (e.g., **LPG** or **CNG** cylinders), whereas **solids** and **liquids** have very low compressibility because their particles are already very close to each other.
</ul

questions.question:
Read the given statements and select the most appropriate option.

**Statements:
A: **Coal and petroleum were formed from the degradation of bio-mass.
**B: **They are exhaustible resources.

options.text: Both statements A and B are correct
Neither statement A nor B is correct

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both statements A and B are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Coal** and **petroleum** are known as **fossil fuels** because they were formed from the **degradation of bio-mass** (the remains of plants and animals) buried deep under the Earth's crust **millions of years** ago. Under conditions of **high pressure** and **high temperature**, the organic matter was converted into these fuels. ***Hence, statement A is correct.***
 
• Natural resources that are available in **limited quantities** and can be depleted through human consumption are categorized as **exhaustible resources**. Since the rate of formation of coal and petroleum is extremely slow compared to the rate of human consumption, they are considered **exhaustible** and **non-renewable**. ***Hence, statement B is correct.***
 
• The formation of **coal** specifically occurred through a process called **carbonization**, where dead vegetation was slowly converted into coal over **300 million years**.
 
• **Petroleum** was formed from **dead organisms** that lived in the sea; as these organisms died, their bodies settled at the bottom and were covered by layers of **sand** and **clay**, eventually transforming into oil and gas.
 
• Because both statements accurately describe the origin and the nature of these resources, the correct choice is that both are valid. ***Hence, the correct answer is Both statements A and B are correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Natural Resources:**
 
 
• **Inexhaustible Natural Resources:** These are present in **unlimited quantities** in nature and are not likely to be exhausted by human activities. Examples include **sunlight** and **air**.
 
• **Exhaustible Natural Resources:** These have a **fixed supply** and include **forests**, **wildlife**, **minerals**, **coal**, **petroleum**, and **natural gas**.
 
 
 
• **Coal and its Products:**
 
 
• **Coke:** A tough, porous, and black substance that is an almost **pure form of carbon**, used in the manufacture of **steel**.
 
• **Coal Tar:** A thick black liquid with an unpleasant smell, used as a starting material for **synthetic dyes**, **drugs**, and **explosives**.
 
• **Coal Gas:** Obtained during the processing of coal to get coke; it was historically used for **street lighting** in **London (1810)** and **New York (1820)**.
 
 
 
• **Petroleum Refining:**
 
 
• **Petroleum** is a dark oily liquid known as **"Black Gold"** due to its high commercial value.
 
• It is a mixture of various constituents such as **petroleum gas**, **petrol**, **diesel**, **lubricating oil**, and **paraffin wax**.
 
• The process of separating these various fractions is called **refining**, which is carried out in a **petroleum refinery**.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact:**
 
 
• The burning of fossil fuels releases **carbon dioxide**, **nitrogen oxides**, and **sulphur oxides**, which contribute to **global warming** and **acid rain**.

questions.question: Each succeeding member of the homologous series of alkane differs from the previous one by a unit that consists of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**one carbon and two hydrogens**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **homologous series** is a sequence of compounds with the same **functional group** and similar chemical properties in which the members of the series differ by a specific structural unit.
 
• In the case of **alkanes**, which are **saturated hydrocarbons** containing only single bonds, the general formula is **CnH2n+2**.
 
• The first member of the alkane series is **methane (CH4)**, and the second member is **ethane (C2H6)**. By subtracting the molecular formula of methane from ethane (C2H6 - CH4), we get a difference of **CH2**.
 
• This **CH2 unit** consists of **one carbon and two hydrogens**. This unit is also known as the **methylene group**. ***Hence, the correct answer is one carbon and two hydrogens.***
 
• Successive members of any homologous series, including **alkenes (CnH2n)** and **alkynes (CnH2n-2)**, always differ by this same **CH2 unit**.
 
• The **molecular mass** of each succeeding member in a homologous series increases by **14 atomic mass units (14u)**, as the atomic mass of **carbon** is **12u** and **hydrogen** is **1u** (12 + 2x1 = 14).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Alkanes:**
 
 
• Alkanes are known as **paraffins** because they have little affinity toward general reagents (low reactivity).
 
• Examples include **Propane (C3H8)**, **Butane (C4H10)**, and **Pentane (C5H12)**. Each subsequent member is formed by adding **one carbon and two hydrogens** to the previous one.
 
• They primarily undergo **substitution reactions** and **combustion**.
 
 
 
• **Physical Properties of Homologous Series:**
 
 
• As the **molecular mass** increases within a series, there is a regular gradation in **physical properties**.
 
• For instance, the **melting point** and **boiling point** of alkanes increase with the increase in the number of **carbon atoms** due to the increase in **Van der Waals forces**.
 
• The **solubility** in a particular solvent also shows a regular gradation as the chain length increases.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Properties:**
 
 
• Members of a **homologous series** exhibit similar **chemical properties** because they possess the same **functional group**.
 
• All **alkanes** react with **oxygen** during **combustion** to produce **carbon dioxide** and **water**.
 
 
 
• **Isomerism:**
 
 
• While the first three members of the alkane series (**methane, ethane, propane**) do not show **structural isomerism**, members from **butane (C4H10)** onwards can exist in different structural forms.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **CH2 unit** is the fundamental building block that distinguishes adjacent members in all **hydrocarbon** series.
 
• In **IUPAC nomenclature**, the suffix **-ane** is used for alkanes, **-ene** for alkenes, and **-yne** for alkynes.
 
• The **general formula** allows for the prediction of the formula of any member; for example, the 10th member of the alkane series (**decane**) has **10 carbon atoms** and (2x10 + 2) = **22 hydrogen atoms**, resulting in **C10H22**.
</ul

questions.question: In which of the following parts of the human body do the epithelial cells have cilia?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Respiratory tract**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ciliated epithelial cells** are specialized **epithelial cells** that possess hair-like protoplasmic outgrowths called **cilia** on their free surface.
 
• In the **human body**, these cells are primarily located in the **Respiratory tract**, including the **nasal passages**, **trachea** (windpipe), and **bronchi**.
 
• The main **function** of the cilia in the **respiratory system** is to move **mucus**, **dust**, and **pathogens** away from the **lungs** and toward the **throat**, where they can be swallowed or expelled.
 
• This rhythmic, wave-like motion is essential for the **mucociliary clearance** mechanism, which serves as a primary defense against **respiratory infections**. ***Hence, the respiratory tract is the correct answer.***
 
• These cells are usually **columnar** or **cuboidal** in shape and are anchored to a **basement membrane**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Buccal Cavity:**
 
 
• The **buccal cavity** (mouth) is lined with **Non-keratinized Stratified Squamous Epithelium**.
 
• This tissue consists of multiple layers of cells designed to protect the underlying structures from **mechanical stress** and **abrasion** caused by **chewing**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Food Pipe (Esophagus):**
 
 
• The **esophagus** is also lined with **non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium**.
 
• The primary role of the **epithelium** here is to provide a smooth surface for the passage of the **bolus** and to protect against the friction of **food particles**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Stomach Wall:**
 
 
• The **stomach wall** is lined with **Simple Columnar Epithelium**.
 
• These cells are specialized for **secretion** and **protection**; they secrete **mucus** to protect the stomach lining from **hydrochloric acid (HCl)** and **digestive enzymes** like **pepsin**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Fallopian Tubes:**
 
 
• Besides the **respiratory tract**, **ciliated epithelium** is also found in the **oviducts** (**Fallopian tubes**) of the **female reproductive system**.
 
• In this **location**, the cilia help in the transport of the **ovum** (egg) from the **ovary** toward the **uterus**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Difference between Cilia and Microvilli:**
 
 
• **Cilia** are involved in **movement** and transport of substances across the cell surface, whereas **microvilli** (found in the **small intestine**) are primarily for increasing the **surface area** for **absorption**.
 
 
 
• **Clinical Significance:**
 
 
• A **genetic disorder** known as **Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia** (**PCD**) or **Kartagener Syndrome** occurs when the cilia fail to move correctly, leading to chronic **sinusitis**, **bronchitis**, and **infertility**.
 
 
 
• **Types of Epithelium:**
 
 
• **Squamous:** Thin, flat cells (e.g., **alveoli** of lungs).
 
• **Cuboidal:** Cube-like cells (e.g., **kidney tubules**).
 
• **Columnar:** Tall, pillar-like cells (e.g., **intestine**).
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which component(s) of blood is/are mainly responsible for transporting food, carbon dioxide and nitrogenous wastes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plasma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Blood** is a connective tissue in fluid form that consists of a fluid medium called **plasma** in which various cells are suspended.
 
• **Plasma** is primarily responsible for the transport of **food** (nutrients like glucose, amino acids, and lipids), **carbon dioxide**, and **nitrogenous wastes** (such as urea) in a dissolved form throughout the body. ***Hence, the correct answer is Plasma.***
 
• It constitutes about **55%** of the total blood volume and is composed of nearly **90-92% water**, with the remaining **8-10%** consisting of proteins, mineral salts, hormones, and waste products.
 
• While **Red Blood Corpuscles (RBCs)** primarily transport **oxygen** using **hemoglobin**, **plasma** carries **carbon dioxide** more efficiently as it is more soluble in water and is often transported in the form of **bicarbonate ions**.
 
• The process of transporting **nitrogenous waste** involves **plasma** carrying substances like **urea** from the **liver** to the **kidneys** for excretion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Red Blood Corpuscles (Erythrocytes):**
 
 
• These are **biconcave** cells that lack a **nucleus** in most mammals to provide more space for **hemoglobin**.
 
• Their primary function is to transport **oxygen** from the lungs to all body tissues and a small amount of **carbon dioxide** back to the lungs.
 
• The average lifespan of an **RBC** is approximately **120 days**, after which they are destroyed in the **spleen**.
 
 
 
• **White Blood Cells (Leukocytes):**
 
 
• These cells act as the body’s **immune system** and help fight against **infections** and foreign particles.
 
• They are divided into **Granulocytes** (Neutrophils, Eosinophils, Basophils) and **Agranulocytes** (Lymphocytes, Monocytes).
 
• They are much fewer in number compared to **RBCs** but can increase rapidly during an **infection** or **inflammation**.
 
 
 
• **Platelets (Thrombocytes):**
 
 
• These are tiny, **cell fragments** produced in the **bone marrow** from **megakaryocytes**.
 
• Their main function is to help in **blood clotting** (coagulation) to prevent excessive bleeding when a blood vessel is injured.
 
• A low count of **platelets** can lead to excessive bleeding, a condition known as **thrombocytopenia**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Plasma Proteins:**
 
 
• **Fibrinogen**: Essential for **blood clotting** or coagulation.
 
• **Globulins**: Primarily involved in the **defense mechanisms** of the body (immunoglobulins).
 
• **Albumins**: Help in maintaining the **osmotic balance** of the blood.
 
 
 
• **Transport Mechanism:** 
 
 
• Nutrients absorbed from the **digestive tract**, such as **glucose** and **fatty acids**, are dissolved in the **plasma** and distributed to cells.
 
• The **pH level** of blood is maintained around **7.4**, which is slightly **alkaline**, largely due to the buffering capacity of **plasma** components.
 
• **Hormones** secreted by **endocrine glands** are also transported via **plasma** to their respective target organs.
 
 
</ul
